capitals.name: Wulei (near Luntai)
capitals.note: 'The protector-general established a general headquarters at Wulei', 350 li east of Kucha; the page offers the Zorkut Ancient City as a candidate site. The coordinates are approximate (about 145 km east of Kucha). The page does not say who sat where between 74 and 90, or at Ban Yong's restoration. Reviewer ea-02-d, 2026-10-19: ends in 22 with the first protectorate (not drawn 23-72); the pages give no seat for 73-90 (Chen Mu's seat undated, Ban Chao's base not named) and Wulei lies outside the 73 and 74-90 keyframes (Loulan, Hotan, Kashgar radii).

correction.text: the Northern and Southern routes of the Western Regions under the protector-general's headquarters at Wulei: the city-states of the Book of Han table, from Beilu and Danhuan to Yutian, with Wulei as the central command

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape before 117. The page dates the protectorate from 'The position of protector-general was officially established in 59 or 60 BCE' (another account has it by 64 BC; the list of protector-generals opens with Zheng Ji, 60-48 BCE) and has the Wusun brought under Han submission in 51 BCE (a vassal event, not part of the shape). 'The post was abandoned after the usurpation of Wang Mang (Xin dynasty) from 8 to 22 CE', but the list runs to Li Chong 13-23 CE, so the shape ends in 22 and the loss is dated 23. The page gives no area figure, so there is no infobox check. The named Tarim Basin plus Turfan-Hami is about 1.02 M km2 by the gazetteer's cells, against 0.27 M km2 for Cliopatria's first Tarim shape (117), which draws only the central oases. Cliopatria's Xiongnu shapes of -66..90 reach 77.7 E (74.7 E in 68-77) from 38.6 N and its Xin shapes of 6-13 reach 73 E, over the same land: the owners of those rows should trim them.

correction.text: Shanshan, whose king sent hostages to Han after Ban Chao killed the Xiongnu envoys

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the first Han foothold after the Wang Mang gap. Ban Chao and 'the small group of delegates slaughtered the Xiongnu envoys and sent their heads to the king' of Shanshan, who then sent hostages to Han (73). The page does not say where Shanshan lay; the Loulan radius is my reading (Shanshan was the Loulan kingdom). The protector-general's post is not yet revived (74, Chen Mu, per the protectorate page).

correction.text: Shanshan (Loulan), Khotan and Kashgar: 'came under Chinese rule by 74 CE'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The kingdoms of Khotan and Kashgar came under Chinese rule by 74 CE.' The protectorate page adds that in 74 CE the post of protector-general was awarded to Chen Mu, who 'was killed by the rebellious troops of Yanqi and Qiuci' (the page does not date his death), so Kucha and Yanqi stay outside. Ban Chao attacked Turpan in 85 and made the Wusun of the Ili his allies (80s), but the page does not say the Han held either, so neither is in the shape. Radii of 150 km around Loulan, Hotan and Kashgar are my reading of 'kingdom'.

correction.text: the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami except Yanqi, with the Protector General at Qiuci (Kucha)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Ban Chao 'was awarded the title of Protector General and stationed at Qiuci' in 91, and 'ultimately brought the whole of the Tarim Basin under Chinese control' (undated); Yanqi was beaten only in 94, so it is cut out until then. The protectorate page says the seat 'was for a time shifted to Taqian (or Tagan; near modern Kucha)'. The date of each oasis between 74 and 94 is not on the pages: the ledger carries the rest-of-the-basin gain at confidence 1.

Ban Chao retired as Protector General in 102 and died within weeks; 'the power of the Xiongnu in the Western Territories increased again'. correction.text: unchanged shape, years 123..175 only: the protectorate restored by Ban Yong (123-124) and the Chief Official of the Western Regions, last seen in 175

keyframe_review.note: The shape (Tarim oases, 272,538 km2 in the table; 238,739 km2 by cells) is not a protectorate from 117. The protectorate was abandoned on 29 July 107 and 'restored from 123 to 124 by the son of Ban Chao, Ban Yong' (protectorate page); the Chief Official page says 'the chief official took over those duties in the latter part of the 2nd century' and that the office was 'last seen in 175', with a 119 appointment aimed at the leftover Xiongnu. So the shape holds for 123 to 175 as the restored protectorate and then the Chief Official's nominal sphere under the Dunhuang governor, not for 117-122 or 176-183. region.text: the Northern and Southern routes of the Western Regions, governed from Wulei

ledger.note: 60 BCE: Zheng Ji becomes the first protector-general of the Western Regions, with headquarters at Wulei. 'The position of protector-general was officially established in 59 or 60 BCE', after the Southern Xiongnu ruler Bi, the Rizhu King of the Right, submitted to the Han; Zheng Ji, who received him, was made protector-general of the Northern and Southern routes; 'another account states that the post of protector-general had already been established by 64 BC'. The page lists Zheng Ji as 60-48 BCE. The Book of Han table of 34 city-states is the page's extent; the basin and Turfan-Hami regions are my reading of it.

region.text: the Wusun nation, 'brought under Han submission'

ledger.note: 51 BCE: the Wusun submit to the Han. 'During the peak of the protectorate's power in 51 BCE, the Wusun nation was brought under Han submission.' The page names no land; Cliopatria's Wusun shape of -66..-51 is my reading.

region.text: the Wusun nation of the Ili

ledger.note: 23 CE: the Wusun tie lapses with the protectorate. The page is silent on the Wusun after 51 BCE; the end date is bridged from the abandonment of the post (the Ban Chao page has the Wusun of the Ili as his allies in the 80s, an alliance, not drawn as vassalage).

region.text: the Western Regions left without a protector-general

ledger.note: 23 CE: the protectorate is abandoned in the Wang Mang years. 'The post was abandoned after the usurpation of Wang Mang (Xin dynasty) from 8 to 22 CE'; the list of protector-generals ends with Li Chong, 13-23 CE, so the loss is dated 23. In 45 CE 'the eighteen states of the Western Regions requested the re-establishment of the protectorate' but Emperor Guangwu refused.

region.text: the Western Regions, contested between Han and Xiongnu

ledger.note: 73: Han and Xiongnu fight for the Western Regions again. 'General Dou Gu embarked on an expedition to attack the Xiongnu' (73) and Ban Chao killed the Xiongnu envoys at Shanshan; the Western Regions page calls the region 'a heavily contested region during the Han-Xiongnu War until 89 AD'. The zone is my reading of 'the Western Regions'.

region.text: Shanshan, whose king sent hostages to Han

ledger.note: 73: Shanshan submits to Ban Chao. He and his delegates 'slaughtered the Xiongnu envoys and sent their heads to the king', who then sent hostages to Han. Shanshan is the Loulan kingdom (my reading; the page does not place it).
74: Khotan comes under Chinese rule. 'The kingdoms of Khotan and Kashgar came under Chinese rule by 74 CE.' The protectorate page adds that in 74 the post of protector-general was awarded to Chen Mu.
74: Kashgar comes under Chinese rule ('by 74 CE', same sentence as Khotan). Ban Chao crushed fresh rebellions in Kashgar in 80 and 87 and in Yarkand in 88.

89: the Han-Xiongnu contest for the Western Regions ends. The region was 'a heavily contested region during the Han-Xiongnu War until 89 AD'. The Ban Chao page adds that after his death in 102 'the power of the Xiongnu in the Western Territories increased again', undated.

region.text: Qiuci (Kucha), where the Protector General was stationed

ledger.note: 91: Ban Chao takes Kucha and the Protector General's seat. He 'was awarded the title of Protector General and stationed at Qiuci' in 91. Qiuci is Kucha; the radius is my reading.

region.text: the Tarim Basin and Turfan-Hami east of Kashgar, except Yanqi and the oases already held

ledger.note: 91: the rest of the Tarim Basin, apart from Yanqi, is drawn as Han. The page says Ban Chao 'ultimately brought the whole of the Tarim Basin under Chinese control' without dating each oasis; 91 is the year of his title. Bridging judgment. Ban Chao page: 'In 91 CE, Ban Chao finally succeeded in pacifying the Western Regions and was awarded the title of Protector General and stationed at Qiuci (Kucha).' (Reviewer ea-02-d, 2026-10-19: confidence raised from 1 to 2 on that sentence.)
91: the Protector General sits at Qiuci (Kucha). The protectorate page has the seat 'for a time shifted to Taqian (or Tagan; near modern Kucha)'; the move from Wulei is undated there.

94: Ban Chao defeats Yanqi and the whole basin submits. 'In 94 CE, Chao proceeded to again attack and defeat Yanqi [Karashahr]'; 'more than fifty kingdoms presented hostages, as submission to the Han dynasty'.

region.text: the Western Regions left without a protector-general

ledger.note: 107: the Qiang rising ends the protectorate. 'On 29 July 107, a series of Qiang uprisings in the areas of Hexi Corridor and Guanzhong'; 'Duan Xi was killed and the post was abandoned'. The Ban Chao page says Xiongnu power in the Western Territories 'increased again' after his death.

region.text: the Western Regions restored under Ban Yong (123-124) and then the Chief Official

ledger.note: 123: Ban Yong restores the protectorate. 'The protectorate was later restored from 123 to 124 by the son of Ban Chao, Ban Yong.' The page gives no land; the Cliopatria shape of 117 is my reading. The Chief Official page has a 119 appointment against the leftover Xiongnu and the office 'last seen in 175'.

region.text: the Chief Official's nominal sphere under the Dunhuang governor

ledger.note: 176: the Han presence in the Tarim ends. The Chief Official was 'last seen in 175' and 'the Eastern Han no longer maintained the post of protector general'; the page does not say the sphere ended then. Bridging judgment: no office is recorded until the Cao Wei revival, so the shape is not drawn for 176-334 (224-305 is covered by the Cao Wei and Western Jin shapes).

region.text: the Tarim oasis states such as Kucha, submitting to Former Liang in 335

ledger.note: 335: Zhang Jun's Former Liang marches across the sands and the oasis states submit. 'In 335 his forces marched across the sands and expanded his territory', forcing 'oasis states such as Kucha' to submit. The protectorate page: 'again revived in 335 by Former Liang'.
335: the revived protectorate is headquartered at Gaochang (Turfan). 'The protectorate was again revived in 335 by Former Liang and headquartered in Gaochang until the demise of Northern Liang.'

region.text: the Gaochang-based protectorate and the oasis states it held

ledger.note: 439: the protectorate ends with the Sixteen Kingdoms. It existed 'on and off from 59 or 60 BCE until the end of the Sixteen Kingdoms period in 439 AD'; the seat at Gaochang lasted 'until the demise of Northern Liang'. The page names no heir; the Tang successor (Protectorate General to Pacify the West) is of the 7th century.

wars.name: Han–Xiongnu War
wars.outcome: The Han under Dou Gu and Ban Chao take Shanshan, Khotan and Kashgar (73-74); the Western Regions are 'a heavily contested region during the Han-Xiongnu War until 89 AD'.
wars.note: The war itself is older and wider; this entry is its Western Regions front only. The war's article was not opened.

wars.name: Ban Chao's conquest of the Tarim Basin

zones.text: the Tarim Basin, 'ultimately' all under Chinese control

wars.outcome: Khotan and Kashgar by 74; rebellions in Kashgar (80, 87) and Yarkand (88) crushed; Ban Chao Protector General at Qiuci in 91; Yanqi defeated in 94 and over fifty kingdoms give hostages.
wars.note: Descriptive name; Wikipedia has no article of this title. Ban Chao's biography is the page.

wars.name: Kushan–Han clash of 90
wars.outcome: The Kushans, refused a Han princess, 'marched on Ban Chao in 90 CE with a force of 70,000 but were defeated by the smaller Chinese force'; no border moved.
wars.note: Descriptive name. In 84 the Kushans had helped Ban Chao against the Kangju.

wars.name: Qiang uprisings of 107
wars.outcome: Qiang risings in the Hexi Corridor and Guanzhong on 29 July 107: Duan Xi was killed and the protectorate abandoned.
wars.note: Descriptive name; the Qiang rebellion article was not opened. The fighting was in the Han heartland, so the Tarim is not a contested zone.

wars.name: Former Liang's expedition into the Tarim

zones.text: the oasis states such as Kucha

wars.outcome: Zhang Jun's forces 'marched across the sands and expanded his territory' in 335; the oasis states such as Kucha submitted and the protectorate was revived at Gaochang.
wars.note: Descriptive name; the page gives no battle.

certainty.note: Every frontier is a desert-oasis reach: the Tarim rim, Turfan-Hami and the Pamir foot are approximate, defined by which city-states submitted. No treaty or survey line exists on the pages; the Book of Han table of 34 city-states is the only list.

notes:
Five pages were opened (the budget for 12 shapes): the protectorate, the Chief Official of the Western Regions, Western Regions (thin), Ban Chao and Former Liang. No infobox or area figure appears on any of them, so no keyframe has an infobox area check.

What this state is. Cliopatria dates the row 117..601; the page dates the protectorate 'on and off from 59 or 60 BCE until the end of the Sixteen Kingdoms period in 439 AD', so the dossier runs -60..439. It is typed colony (a Han, later Wei, Jin and Liang administrative reach over the Tarim city-states, drawn as a vassal tint of the metropole). Overlords by era, from the pages: Han (-60..8), Xin (9..23: Dan Qin and Li Chong served under Wang Mang, 'the usurpation of Wang Mang (Xin dynasty)'), Han again (73..175), Cao Wei and Western Jin (Chief Official 'until around 328', drawn by their own Cliopatria shapes in 224-305), Former Liang (335..376), then the page names no holder until Northern Liang (to 439). Drawn only where a page records a protector-general or chief official: -60..22; 73..106; 123..175; 335..439. Not drawn: 23..72 (Wang Mang gap; 45 CE refusal), 107..122 (abandoned 29 July 107), 176..334 (nominal Chief Official, Wei/Jin shapes cover 224-305), and 440..601 (Cliopatria rows 451-601 are wrong: the page ends the protectorate in 439).

Settled against the pages: 60 BCE start (Zheng Ji, Wulei), 51 BCE Wusun, Wang Mang gap, 74 Khotan and Kashgar, 91 Qiuci, 94 Yanqi, 107 abandonment, 123-124 Ban Yong, 335 Gaochang revival, 439 end.

Not settled:
- The pages disagree on the Wang Mang gap: prose says 'abandoned ... from 8 to 22 CE' while the list gives Dan Qin 1-13 and Li Chong 13-23; the loss is dated 23. Month and place of Chen Mu's death (74-75) are not given.
- Between 74 and 94 the order in which the oases fell is not on the pages: the rest-of-the-basin gain of 91 is confidence 1. The 176 loss (Chief Official 'last seen in 175') and the 23 end of the Wusun tie are confidence 1.
- Who held the Tarim 376-397, and what happened at Gaochang 439-460, is not on any page opened: Northern Liang, Former Qin, Later Liang, Cao Wei, Western Jin pages were not opened (budget). Cliopatria's 387 west-edge cut, 476 east-edge cut and 561 west re-expansion have no page; the 387 shape is kept 'unverified: page budget'.
- Wulei's coordinates (84.4 E, 41.8 N) are an estimate from '350 li east of Kucha'; the page offers the Zorkut Ancient City as a candidate.

Overlaps for other owners. Cliopatria's Xiongnu shapes of -66..90 reach 77.7 E (74.7 E in 68-77) from 38.6 N, i.e. the western Tarim, while the protectorate page has the Han there from 60 BCE; its Han Dynasty shape of 106-116, Xin shape of 6-13 and Cao Wei/Western Jin shapes of 224-305 reach 73 E; the Kushan Empire shapes of 117-183 reach 90.7 E and of 184-237 reach 84.5 E over the Tarim, and the Ban Chao page records only a failed Kushan march in 90 and Kushan help against the Kangju in 84. ia-01 and sa-02 should decide those rows; the seed lists the Rouran Khaganate (to 554), White Huns (410-560), Göktürks (from 555), Tuyuhun and Wusun as neighbours of this dossier's wrong shapes of 451-601.

States Cliopatria lacks that this dossier names as counterparts: Shanshan (Loulan), Khotan (the ancient kingdom; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Khotan is 888-1009 and the existing kingdom-of-khotan dossier is 851-1006), Shule (Kashgar), Yanqi (Karashahr), Jushi (Turpan side). kingdom-of-kucha exists (-150..648) and is used as the Kucha counterpart. 'Tarim city-states' is the counterpart string for the oases taken as a group. The Tang successor (Protectorate General to Pacify the West, 7th century) belongs to the Tang dossier and the Anxi group.

Gazetteer: 'Loulan' is not in places.jsonl (Shanshan kingdom, about 89.9 E, 40.5 N); 'Wulei' is only in capitals. The named Tarim Basin plus Turfan-Hami is about 1.02 M km2, Cliopatria's Tarim rows 0.27-0.70 M km2.
